summary:
READY_AFTER_FIXES. The rule itself survived round two: I re-checked the machinery it rests on and found nothing that breaks it. `Function_Common.retrieve_function_data` is `Item_Net.retrieve` over `(term * info)` with `(map o apsnd) (transform_function_data (Morphism.transfer_morphism' ctxt))` (function_common.ML:278-281), so it needs a `Proof.context` (`get_functions = #2 o Data.get o Context.Proof`, :278) and returns the key term untransformed; `info` really carries `simps: thm list option` beside `psimps: thm list` (:22-23); `Item_Net.update` removes-then-conses on `op aconv o apply2 fst` (:261, item_net.ML:71), so the `termination` flip leaves exactly one entry; the psimps premise really is `Wellfounded.accp` built in ML (function_common.ML:132-134) with `<f>_dom` only an abbreviation afterwards. Under MERGE nothing is counted twice, for the reason def-2 gives rather than the one PLAN.md:111 gives.

What blocks a clean 开工 is not the rule but four things the plan currently asserts and cannot support. (1) §7's per-target claims are unmeasured and one of them is stated as "confirmed": named_target.ML:108 (locale) and :116 (class) both route through `Generic_Target.locale_declaration`, and with `pervasive = false` (function.ML:135, :215) that means `locale_target_declaration` + `standard_declaration` and NO `background_declaration` (generic_target.ML:465-468, :428-429) — the very argument PLAN.md:63-67 uses to call a locale-target `fun` a limitation-#6 case applies verbatim to the class target that PLAN.md:238-240 says is unaffected, and the probe it cites ("§7 item 2") does not exist. (2) Two sentences name guards that cannot fail: Test_All.thy:113-128 calls one `run ()` twice over a fixed `all` (:40) and fixed `env` (:46) through a pure path, and after `normalize` is deleted the rewritten S3e/S8 contain zero references to `Semantic_Digest` (their only call today is :122 and :194) and compare hand-built raw terms. (3) Nothing in §6 or §9 distinguishes MERGE from replace — the decision the user changed after round one ships with no assertion of its own. (4) §9 item 3 puts the pass/fail line on an LLM verdict the change does not control, while its free step (ii) names an observable (a seed SET) that no component emits — `interpret_file` returns `len(seeds)` (semantic_interpretation.py:1757-1759) and `Semantic_Store.dry_run` returns `string list * int` (semantic_store.ML:67).

All three implementer choices are accepted. Eight fixes, two rejections, five proposals for the user. None of the fixes touches F1–F7 or changes the rule; def-1 is the only one whose outcome can change what gets implemented, which is why it should run first.

rulings.title: §2's statement of what the registry query returns is incomplete: Net.matching also hands back the whole top-level wildcard branch
rulings.reason: Mechanism verified independently. net.ML:188-209 `matching`: for a query whose head is neither Var nor Abs the final branch is `| _ => rands t (net, var::nets)  (*var could match also*)` (net.ML:208), and `add_key_of_terms` keys any Var/Abs-headed term as the single `VarK` (net.ML:53-62); `Item_Net.retrieve = order_list o Net.unify_term net` (item_net.ML:47). So an atomic query does return the root wildcard branch as well. But the headline is withdrawn: PLAN.md:59-63 and :140-142 are INCLUSION statements ('every entry keyed on a bare Const of that name comes back') and both are true — the bullet omits the complement, it does not assert a falsehood. Both rebuttals are right that the finding's proposed `#fs` filter is the wrong component: `retrieve_function_data` transforms only the second component (`(map o apsnd) ...`, function_common.ML:279-281), so the key term comes back raw as `fst` and the implementer must strip it anyway — guard the key, not the block. Both are also right that the filter is not an unconditional invariant: a `rewrites`-renamed key whose head is the queried constant still passes. I keep the guard anyway on the elegance rule (CLAUDE.md: a shape that makes an invariant impossible to violate beats one that asks people to remember it), and because the file already applies exactly this discipline five lines above — `spec_rule_axioms` re-checks the Item_Net answer against the item's own content (`mentions_const`, semantic_digest.ML:374-381). Verified the guard breaks nothing the plan relies on: a mutual block keys one entry per element of `fs` (function_common.ML:286), each head `Const`; an overloading family keys two bare `Const`s of the same name at different types; a locale-target entry is comb-keyed and never reached by an atomic query at all.
rulings.fix: Three hand edits in PLAN.md. (1) :59-63 — cite net.ML:188-209 beside :53-62 and state both branches: an atomic query returns every entry keyed on the atom `c` at any type (net.ML:193) PLUS the whole top-level wildcard branch (net.ML:208), which holds any entry whose key term has a Var or Abs head (net.ML:59-61); the key is the morphism image of the `fs` element (function_common.ML:286, :106-121), hence a bare `Const` only when no term-rewriting mixin intervened. (2) :140-142 — the same correction, and fix the return type: `retrieve_function_data` yields `(term * info) list`, the `term` being the net's key, untouched by the transfer morphism (function_common.ML:261, :279-281). (3) §4 implementation notes — one line on the key: `|> filter (fn (t, _) => case head_of t of Const (n, _) => n = c | _ => false) |> map snd`, with the comment 'the net also returns its wildcard branch; keep only entries the net indexed under this constant'. Describe it as 'drops wildcard-keyed entries', never as an unconditional invariant.

rulings.title: Nothing in the proposed test set pins F2's MERGE half — every §6 assertion passes equally under "replace"
rulings.reason: The most important finding of the round, and I could not break it. The three positive §6 assertions (PLAN.md:208-213) are all of the form 'some prop mentions X', satisfied by the registry equations alone; the three controls (:214-216) only assert the branch does NOT fire. Nothing outside §6 helps: Test_All.thy:110-137 asserts determinism (blind by construction), coverage and non-zero edges — replace is perfectly deterministic; §9 item 2 records info COUNTS; §9 item 3's subjects `narquil` and `galmuth` are plain top-level `fun`s with no sibling `definition`, so both move under replace too. The consequence is a regression against TODAY's behaviour, not a lost improvement: today `own_defining_axioms` returns every same-theory-surviving `Defs` axiom (semantic_digest.ML:387-399), and the shape is shipped — I read afp-2026-05-13/thys/Amortized_Complexity/Pairing_Heap_List2_Analysis.thy:22-40 and `consts sz` (:22) sits in the SAME theory as an `overloading` block holding `fun size_hps` (:30-32) beside `definition size_hp` (:34-35, body `sz(hps h) + 1`) and `definition size_heap` (:37-38). The plan's own standard supports the finding: for change 2 it deliberately negates S8 'so that nobody quietly reintroduces the normaliser' (:189-190), while the half of F2 the user revised gets no equivalent. I accept both rebuttals' convergent assertion over the finding's own: a `fun` simp is `Trueprop (f x = …)` and can never satisfy `Logic.dest_equals`, while the surviving `Defs` axiom is a Pure meta-equality (VERIFICATION.md §2 row 1, `narquil ≡ narquil_sumC`), so the structural form fails today, fails under replace, and also pins PLAN.md:30's 'nothing is filtered by name' — which the finding's `_sumC` string form does not. Fix part (b), the new `overloading` test subject, is rejected as a blocking test: it exercises no branch part (a) does not (the merge is one expression), and the same-theory overloading family has never been measured — VERIFICATION.md row 8 put `consts dworl` in the PARENT theory, so `same_theory` emptied ② and ③ could not fire there.
rulings.fix: Add to the new §6 subsection, on the `sens_fun` subject the plan already declares, one assertion that `own_defining_axioms env "Test_Sensitivity.sens_fun"` contains BOTH (i) a prop that is a Pure meta-equality (`exists (can Logic.dest_equals) ps`) and (ii) a prop that is not (`exists (not o can Logic.dest_equals) ps`) — equivalently (ii) as 'mentions Orderings.ord_class.less'. It FAILS today (the sole prop is the meta-equality), PASSES under merge, FAILS under replace, FAILS under a `_sumC` name filter. Repeat it on `sens_pfun` at zero cost. Separately, do NOT add the `overloading` test subject; instead add the same-theory `consts` + `overloading` family (the `sz` shape) as one row of the pre-flight census of def-1, and promote it to a §6 subject only if the census shows ③ actually fires there.

rulings.title: Acceptance step (ii) as written cannot be observed: the dry run reports a seed COUNT, never the seed set
rulings.reason: Factually correct and verified: `interpret_file`'s dry-run path logs '%d of %d entries are seeds' and returns `len(seeds)` (semantic_interpretation.py:1757-1759); `Semantic_Store.dry_run : bool -> Context.generic list -> string list * int` (semantic_store.ML:67) yields work-theory names plus one int. So PLAN.md:290-293's criterion names an object no component emits, in a PAID acceptance. But the framing 'the only step that proves the seed reason' is refuted: per-entity attribution is produced, entity-labelled and free, inside step (iii) — `verdict: %s same=%s` (semantic_interpretation.py:990) and `gate: %s CHANGED by the prefilter` (:1450), which is exactly how acceptance_step10/REPORT.md built its per-root table. In this scaffold such a line can only mean 'seed': the gate runs on seeds plus dependents enrolled by an upstream CHANGED verdict, and neither `narquil` nor `galmuth` depends on any other edited root. Both rebuttals' repair is better than the finding's, which also is not executable as written — `gate_inspect.py` prints the BOOLEAN `semantic_digest is not None`, not the digest. Severity drops to editorial: one sentence of a free pre-check, no design consequence.
rulings.fix: In PLAN.md §9 item 3, split the criterion between (ii) and (iii). (ii) becomes the go/no-go on the one number that exists: the dry run's N must rise above the 26 recorded for the same A1→B transition in ai-artifacts/acceptance_step10/REPORT.md run 2; the count does not attribute, and if N does not rise, stop before paying for (iii). (iii) carries the attribution: the host log must show a `gate:` or `verdict:` line naming `constant Sim_Measure_A1.narquil` and one naming `constant Sim_Measure_A1.galmuth` (semantic_interpretation.py:990, :1450); neither can be produced for an entity the scan did not send, and neither has an enrolment route in this scaffold. Do not write 'is a seed = the digest differs': the seed test has three independent routes (digest, dep set, eff*), semantic_interpretation.py:1702-1721.

rulings.title: "galmuth judged UNCHANGED" is a pass/fail criterion of an ~USD 11 run that the change under test does not control
rulings.reason: The mechanism is exactly as described and the direction of the flake is the real point. `_gate` rules CHANGED below `_GATE_SIMILARITY` (semantic_interpretation.py:1447-1451) and otherwise needs the judge to answer 'same' (:1452-1455), and `_judge`'s docstring is explicit that 'no verdict after the one extra ask, a FatalAgentError, any failure of the session — reads as CHANGED' (:1327-1330). The gate is deliberately fail-safe, so putting 'judged UNCHANGED' in a list under the heading 'Acceptance' uses that asymmetry backwards: the acceptance can be broken by the design working as specified. The finding cites the wrong number for the risk (plerx's 0.897 is a genuinely changed entity clearing the bar downward), and the right one — galmuth's own measured 0.9472 against 6/85 no-change pairs falling below 0.90 in ai-artifacts/similarity_measurement/REPORT.md — makes the risk low single digits rather than a coin toss, so severity drops. The finding's own proposed criterion ('narquil judged CHANGED') is LLM-decided too, but defensibly so, and that asymmetry should be written down rather than left implicit. The second half of the finding is right and I verified it: galmuth is unary over `nat list`, so its `Defs` axiom is the variable-free `galmuth ≡ galmuth_sumC` (VERIFICATION.md §2 row 1 shows the unary shape) — removing the normaliser alone moves nothing; and VERIFICATION.md:274 measured galmuth's digest under direction A WITH the normaliser as identical in A and B — change 1 alone moves nothing either. Both changes are needed, and the plan credits F6′ alone.
rulings.fix: Rewrite PLAN.md:290-296. Pass/fail in (iii): `narquil` judged CHANGED and minted, with `narquil_small`/`narquil_large`/`narquil_glaive_*` re-interpreted or their `interpreted_at` raised — the direct repair of acceptance_step10/REPORT.md finding 1 — plus one clause saying why that verdict is a safe criterion while galmuth's is not: every failure mode of the gate reads CHANGED (semantic_interpretation.py:1327-1330, :1445/:1449/:1455), so the narquil criterion fails only if the gate affirmatively agrees the two texts are the same, which would be a gate finding rather than a refutation of this change. Demote galmuth's verdict to an observation recorded in ACCEPTANCE.md with its prefilter cosine and, if reached, the judge's sentence — it is the first live sample of the UNCHANGED path, which acceptance_step10/REPORT.md finding 3 records as never exercised, and it is worth having whichever way it falls. While there, correct the parenthetical at :291-292: galmuth's digest moves because change 1 puts the renamed pattern variables into the payload AND F6′ stops them being normalised away; neither alone suffices (VERIFICATION.md:274, §2 row 1).

rulings.title: §5 names Test_All's determinism check as the guard for change 2, but that check cannot fail
rulings.reason: The core is undeniable and I verified every line. Test_All.thy:113 binds `fun run () = map (fn e => Semantic_Digest.semantics_of env e) all` over `all` fixed at :40 and `env` fixed at :46, calls it at :115 and :117 and compares at :128 — one in-process pass repeated, not 'same source twice'. `semantics_of` is a pure read of theory data and `digest_term` bottoms out in `Term_Digest.term128`, a pure FNV fold whose only mutable state (the thm128 cache) is not on this path, so `r1 = r2` holds by construction with the normaliser and without it. The project's own documents already say a content-blind digest passes determinism and coverage (archive/plans/CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:715; doc/invalidation_limitations.md:203). Two things do not survive. First, 'change 2 ships with NO regression guard' overstates: §9 item 3 (ii) requires `galmuth` to become a seed, and that is a genuine two-sided end-to-end discriminator — acceptance_step10/REPORT.md finding 3 records that with a normalised digest galmuth was NOT a seed, and VERIFICATION.md:274 measured its digest as unmoved under change 1 with the normaliser in place, so a surviving normaliser fails step (ii). It is a paid, one-shot discriminator, not a standing in-suite guard. Second, the proposed 'the seed set must be EXACTLY that set' tightening is refuted by measurement: acceptance_step10/REPORT.md records N = 26 for six edited roots, most of them uncached statement-keyed theorems, so exact equality would fail a correct implementation. Writing a known-false criterion into an acceptance is worse than the containment criterion the plan has.
rulings.fix: Edit PLAN.md:190-191 by hand: drop 'and is the guard for change 2' and restate the Test_All block as what it asserts — one in-process pass repeated over the same `all` and `env`, green with and without the normaliser; what it contributes is the no-crash / coverage / non-zero-edges half. Then name the guards that do discriminate: whatever in-suite assertion elegance-2 settles on, and §9 item 3 (ii)'s requirement that `galmuth` appear in the seed set, which is two-sided against the step-10 record where it did not. Do NOT adopt the 'exactly that set' tightening; use the delta wording of merge-3 instead.

rulings.title: §1's stated cost of a cosmetic rename omits the re-interpretation, and the no-baseline row
rulings.reason: Both halves survive, each as one clause, and the two rebuttals between them locate the right two edits. On the first half: the gate's own input is 'a tracked entity E just re-interpreted' (ai-artifacts/SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:131), and the seed set is what gets sent to the LLM, so PLAN.md:35-38's 'only sends the entity through the gate' and 'its only benefit — saving that gate call' understate the cost by a full re-interpretation per renamed entity, and §9 of the same document contradicts §1 by predicting galmuth is re-interpreted inside a live run. On the second half, I part company with the finding's framing but not with its substance: the no-baseline path IS already in the plan, correctly, at PLAN.md:92-98 (forced CHANGED, no prefilter, no judge, mints, enrols), so 'the plan's statement of what it costs is wrong' is refuted there. What the finding got wrong in its premise — that §5:196-198 copies §1's cost — hides a real defect with the sign flipped: the sentence §5 proposes to WRITE into doc/invalidation_limitations.md, 'cosmetic edits (renames) reach the gate and are answered UNCHANGED by the judge', is unconditionally false for a record that predates the gate (semantic_interpretation.py:1445-1447 forces CHANGED with no judge at all), and PLAN.md:97-98 records that the number of such WIP-keyed records is not measured. The register would then carry a stronger claim than the plan itself makes.
rulings.fix: Two hand edits. (1) PLAN.md:35-38: 'only sends the entity through the gate' → 'makes the entity a seed: one re-interpretation, then the prefilter and the judge, which answers UNCHANGED and walls the dependents'; 'saving that gate call' → 'saving that re-interpretation and gate call' (cost anchors if wanted: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md D3 :110 and acceptance_step10/REPORT.md's per-entity figure). (2) PLAN.md:196-198: give the sentence to be written into the register its exception — a rename now moves the digest, so the entity becomes a seed, is re-interpreted once and judged, answered UNCHANGED and walling its dependents WHEN the record carries a baseline; a record predating the gate (digest, no baseline) is forced CHANGED and mints (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md §3 row 2, as PLAN.md:92-98 already records). That is the designed path, not a defect.

rulings.title: §5's list of statements to repair is incomplete
rulings.reason: Two of the six sub-items survive; the other four do not, and both rebuttals independently surfaced a seventh site the finding missed. SURVIVES (a): archive/plans/CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:349 heads §7.3 '（历经实测的四条）' over four items at :350/:358/:359/:361, and PLAN.md:192 deletes item 3 — the heading and the numbering must move with it; this is arithmetic on a document §5 edits in the same sentence. SURVIVES (b): the §14 table header is `| 断言 | 缺了会怎样 |` (:718) and the row at :732 is `| 参数置换 vs 参数改名 | 参数未与 body 同步归一化 |`, while PLAN.md:193-194 supplies assertion-shaped replacement text only — the right cell names a failure mode that cannot occur once nothing is normalised, so the row must be rewritten in both cells or deleted. REJECTED (c) digests.py: a finished phase-2 measurement script, not run by §9 item 3, whose setup (acceptance_step10/REPORT.md:31-33) copies the .thy files and runs the pipeline. REJECTED (d): PLAN.md:231 already schedules the handoff, and that bullet is being replaced wholesale anyway since it still says ③ 'REPLACES' the Defs axiom, which F2 revoked. REJECTED (f): §5:176-179 deletes the whole alpha-normalisation section; splitting its banner from its commentary is the 'consider adding a comment' class. On (e), VERIFICATION.md is a dated measurement record already flagged as superseded at PLAN.md:8-10; annotating it in place is the wrong move — mutating the evidence to track later decisions is how you lose the ability to trust it. ADDED: Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:318, the record-schema comment '(ML-side Semantic_Digest; alpha-canonical)', is the only such claim in production Python (grep confirms one hit) and §5 does not list it.
rulings.fix: Extend PLAN.md §5 by three clauses, by hand. (1) In the CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN bullet: 'delete §7.3 item 3, change the §7.3 heading at :349 from 四条 to 三条, and renumber the present item 4 (:361) to 3'. (2) Make explicit that BOTH cells of the §14 row at :732 are rewritten (or the row deleted, per elegance-2's option (a)). (3) Add Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/semantics.py:318 to the site list — 'alpha-canonical' comes out of the record-schema comment. Separately extend the NOTE at PLAN.md:8-10 by one clause: VERIFICATION.md §4's remedy at :296-303 ('sorting the normalised props') is superseded by F6′ and the current ruling is PLAN.md §2 :99-104. Do not edit VERIFICATION.md itself.

rulings.title: After the normaliser is removed, S3e and S8 call no production code at all; the claimed "nobody quietly reintroduces the normaliser" guard does not exist
rulings.reason: Verified independently and it stands. Test_Sensitivity.thy:108-126 rebuilds sem_locale's payload by hand and Test_Sensitivity.thy:189-203 rebuilds sem_type's parameter payload; the `Const ("Semantic_Digest.nil", …)` and `Const ("Semantic_Digest.typ", …)` nodes are string literals, not calls. The single reference into the module under test is `Semantic_Digest.normalize` at :122 and :194. Delete it (PLAN.md:176-178) and all three assertions are true of raw ML terms whatever `digest_term` does — precisely rule (a) the file states at :12-15, 'an assertion must not be satisfiable through an unrelated path', a rule the file records as having hidden a real defect for a full round. I checked for an escape and there is none: no golden digest is stored anywhere in Test/, S7/S10c/S11c compare digests for EQUALITY (invariant under adding or removing a deterministic pre-hash transform), and Test_All's determinism check is blind by construction. Restoring `fun digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 (normalize t)` (semantic_digest.ML:178) would leave the whole suite green while moving every WIP name-addressed digest in the store. So PLAN.md:189-190 claims a guard the specified rewrite cannot provide, and the specified rewrite must not ship. I note two documentation sites §5 misses that go with it: the S8 subsection title at Test_Sensitivity.thy:182 ('parameters share the body's canonicalisation') and the S3e block comment at :99-107, whose whole subject is a function that will not exist. On the shape, exporting the hasher is net-zero signature growth — `val normalize` (semantic_digest.ML:46-48) is being deleted — and reuses the file's own sanctioned test-only export pattern (`own_defining_axioms`, 'exposed for the sensitivity suite', :63-65); `Term_Digest.digest128` is an equality type so `<>` works directly.
rulings.fix: Delete the claim at PLAN.md:189-191 either way, then pick one of two honest shapes (implementer's call under F7, re-read at §9 item 4). (a) Delete S3e (Test_Sensitivity.thy:99-127) and S8 (:182-204) with their now-unused subjects (:68-69, :184-187), delete the §14 row at CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:732 rather than rewording it, and say plainly in §5 that change 2 keeps no standing in-suite guard, its discriminator being §9 item 3 (ii). (b) Add `val digest_term: term -> Term_Digest.digest128` to SEMANTIC_DIGEST (the function exists at semantic_digest.ML:178) and keep ONE assertion that binds to it — either `digest_term (payload over TFree "a") <> digest_term (the same over TFree "b")`, or the stronger and simpler `digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 t` for a `t` containing a Free and a TFree, which pins 'the digest hashes the term as given' against ANY pre-hash transform rather than this one only. If S3e/S8 survive in any form, also fix the subsection title at :182 and the block comment at :99-107. Do not ship the rewrite specified at PLAN.md:186-190.

rulings.title: The rename note is routed to a register whose stated scope is the opposite polarity
rulings.reason: Both of the finding's load-bearing premises are false, and its concrete consequence is manufactured from a placement the plan never specifies. First: PLAN.md:196-198 says 'one sentence each', and this very plan uses a different, explicit idiom when it wants an entry — 'a new numbered entry (with an index row)' at :225-226, four lines away, and 'part of an existing entry' at :230 ('#6 gets the one sentence…'). The index table's 严重度/影响范围 columns are only a problem for an entry the plan does not ask for. Second: 'all seven entries are missed invalidations' is false. I read doc/invalidation_limitations.md: entry #3 (class 超类传递闭包会被下游污染, :131-146) is over-invalidation plus forward-pointing edges, and it carries a 处理（已落地）section saying the digest does not drift and the edges are tolerated by design — a case closed, yet it holds index row :25. Entry #2 carries an explicit 部分正确性 section. The file also holds substantial non-numbered explanatory prose (:194-223) with no index row and no severity. So a one-sentence non-defect remark is neither foreign to this register nor forced into the index table. What is left is 'name the destination paragraph', which is the 'consider adding a comment' class SCOPE.md:96 tells me to reject. Rejected as a nitpick built on a misreading.
rulings.fix: None. If the user wants the residual ambiguity closed at zero cost, PLAN.md:196-198 can name the host paragraph the way the plan already does elsewhere (a sentence inside entry #7, no new numbered entry, no index row); that is wording, not design, and is the implementer's under F7.

rulings.title: PROPOSAL: the registry carries `input_eqns`, a uniform source that would delete the simps/psimps branch and three of §7's accepted blind spots
rulings.reason: Honestly labelled, competently grounded, and it surfaced a field nothing in this repository mentions — but it must not be adopted, and I verified why. The field is real (`input_eqns: term list`, function_common.ML:29, :104, mapped by the morphism at :120, written identically at function.ML:128 and :210). The disqualifier is where it comes from: function.ML:74-81 takes it from `spec0`, the user's spec, BEFORE `get_preproc` (:78) runs. For `fun` / `function (sequential)` the preprocessor is what disambiguates overlapping clauses — VERIFICATION.md §2 row 6 measured `kraldo` yielding 3 disambiguated rules from the written clauses. With F6′ keeping the sort of a constant's props (PLAN.md:39), swapping two overlapping sequential clauses — which genuinely changes the function's value — would leave `input_eqns` a permutation of itself and the digest unmoved. That is the exact failure class the plan exists to remove (PLAN.md:19-22), reintroduced in the commonest `fun` shape. Two of the four claimed removals also fail: the `accp`/`<f>_rel` edges are not a blind spot but the discriminator the plan's own psimps test uses (PLAN.md:211-213), and the diamond-import bullet ends '(production is never in that env)', so it buys zero. The termination-flip invariance is unproven and specifically doubtful, since that path re-registers through an instantiate morphism derived from an `import_terms`-freshened key (function_common.ML:310-326, applied to the terms at :120) — with the normaliser gone, any resulting type-variable renaming moves the digest anyway. Finally the field is write-only: grep finds no reader in the distribution or the shipped AFP, and it does not exist at all in contrib/Isabelle2024/src/. Keep F3.
rulings.fix: No change required. Optionally, one hand-written sentence in §7 or §8 recording the rejection so the next reviewer cannot re-raise it, with both reasons: `input_eqns` is the user's spec taken before the sequential preprocessor (function.ML:74-81 vs fun.ML:110-140), so with the sort kept it cannot see a reorder of overlapping clauses (VERIFICATION.md §2 row 6); and its invariance across a `termination` flip is not established. Implementer's call under F7.

rulings.title: §7's per-target claims are unmeasured on the registry, and the census that would settle them is scheduled AFTER implementation
rulings.reason: I verified the routing and the defender is right. `add_function_data` is installed by `Local_Theory.declaration {syntax = false, pervasive = false, …}` (function.ML:135, :215). `Generic_Target.locale_declaration` is `pervasive ? background_declaration decl #> locale_target_declaration … #> standard_declaration …` (generic_target.ML:465-468), so with pervasive = false nothing reaches the background theory directly — and named_target.ML:108 (Locale) and :116 (Class) BOTH use it, while only the theory target (:99), `overloading` (overloading.ML:212) and `instantiation` (class.ML:733) use `theory_declaration`, which always calls `background_declaration` (generic_target.ML:428-429). So the argument PLAN.md:63-67 uses to declare a locale-target `fun` a limitation-#6 case applies verbatim to a class-target `fun`, yet PLAN.md:238-240 gives the class target the opposite outcome and says 'confirmed by §7 item 2's probe'. §7 has no numbered items and no probe has been taken: the census is §9 item 2, explicitly at implementation time. Nor can the measurement be borrowed from VERIFICATION.md, because `Spec_Rules.add` uses pervasive = true — the flag IS the difference between the two sources, and PLAN.md:8-10 already concedes the structural rows were taken on Spec_Rules. The stakes are concrete: `Bit_Operations.linordered_euclidean_semiring_bit_operations_class.or_num` is one of the 20 record-eligible constants this change exists to fix (VERIFICATION.md §5), and PLAN.md:284 expects it to 'return its 9 simps' — a figure VERIFICATION.md §4(c) measured on the LOCALE-LEVEL TWIN, whose rules each carry the class predicate and mention all 22 class parameters, while the `_class.`-qualified sibling was the one with clean rules. So the acceptance's expected value conflates two siblings on top of being unmeasured. This does not change the rule, but it can change §7's contents and the acceptance's expectations, so SCOPE's 'measurements that cannot change the design' does not apply.
rulings.fix: Move §9 item 2's census from implementation time to a pre-flight step and widen it from a per-constant info count to the target shapes. For each of (a) a theory-level `fun`, (b) a `fun` in a locale with a `global_interpretation` (the shipped `Bit_Operations.fold2_bit_int.F`), (c) a `fun` in a class body — BOTH `…_class.or_num` and the locale twin `…bit_operations.or_num`, named separately, (d) a `fun` under `overloading`, (e) a `fun` under `instantiation`, and (f) a same-theory `consts` + `overloading` family mixing a `fun` with `definition`s (the `sz` shape of PLAN.md:129-132, which merge-2 and def-2 also need), record: how many infos `Function_Common.retrieve_function_data ctxt (Const (c, T))` returns, the HEAD of each returned key term, and the propositions of the chosen `simps`/`psimps`. Then rewrite §7's first bullet and §9 item 2's expected values from that table, say which of the 20 record-eligible constants ③ actually reaches, drop 'confirmed by', and repoint the two dangling '§7 item 2' references (PLAN.md:10, :240) to §9 item 2. One REPL evaluation, no `isabelle build`, no LMDB.

rulings.title: F2's recorded justification is contradicted by the plan's own headline example eighteen lines later
rulings.reason: Correct and worth one sentence. PLAN.md:111 records the reason merge is safe as 'under the registry source no constant has both a body-carrying `Defs` axiom and registry equations', and PLAN.md:129-132 then cites the case merge exists to serve: the same-theory `overloading` family `sz`. I read afp-2026-05-13/thys/Amortized_Complexity/Pairing_Heap_List2_Analysis.thy — `consts sz` at :22, one `overloading` block at :25-40 holding `fun size_hps` (:30-32) and two body-carrying `definition`s (:34-38), all in one theory, so `same_theory` keeps all three `Defs` axioms. Either ③ fires for `sz`, in which case :111's premise is false on the very constant :131 cites, or ③ does not fire, in which case the §4 example is wrong — and which it is has never been measured (VERIFICATION.md row 8 is the cross-theory variant, where `dworl` is declared in the PARENT theory and ② is empty). The conclusion still holds but for a different reason, and the difference is what a future reader will use as a test: the recorded test would wrongly reject `sz`, and would wrongly accept a future package that registers equations for a constant whose own body-carrying axiom covers the same instance.
rulings.fix: Rewrite the middle clause of PLAN.md:111 to the reason that is actually load-bearing: the function package's own `Defs` axiom is body-free in every variant measured (VERIFICATION.md §2, rows 1-8 and 15) and the registry has only the two writers at function.ML:136 and :216, so a body-carrying `Defs` axiom and a registry equation can never come from the same definitional act — a constant may hold both (the `sz` family does) but they then cover different type instances and nothing is duplicated. No change to the decision.

rulings.title: Three internal cross-references in PLAN.md point at nothing
rulings.reason: All three verified. PLAN.md:10 ('§7 item 2 re-takes them') and :240 ('confirmed by §7 item 2's probe') point at a non-existent target: §7 (:233-260) is an unnumbered bullet list and the census re-take is §9 item 2 (:280-285). PLAN.md:98 says the WIP-keyed record count is 'NOT measured (§8)', but §8 (:262-272) is 'Items decided by the user on 2026-09-13' and holds exactly two bullets, the type-conjunct withdrawal and the paid acceptance — neither mentions the count, so the one unmeasured quantity of change 2's cost model is flagged as recorded somewhere and is recorded nowhere. In a document that is simultaneously the decision record and the implementation instruction, a pointer that does not resolve is a real if small defect, and :240's is substantive rather than clerical (see def-1).
rulings.fix: Hand-edit: repoint :10 and :240 to §9 item 2 and drop ':240's 'confirmed by' until that probe has run; for :98 either add the WIP-keyed-record count to §8 as an explicitly accepted unknown, or drop the '(§8)' and say in place that the count is not measured and the plan does not require it.

rulings.title: §9 item 1 credits Test_All.thy with a cost check it does not perform
rulings.reason: Verified. PLAN.md:279 says 'Test/Test_All.thy (coverage, cost, determinism) passes'. In Test_All.thy:110-137 the timing is printed (`writeln ("  " ^ Timing.message res)`, :124) and compared to nothing; the three hard errors are the determinism comparison (:128-129, which cannot fail — see normaliser-1), resolution coverage below 95% (:133-135), and `edges > 0 andalso with_digest > 0` (:136-137). So what item 1 actually buys is 'nothing crashes, ≥95% of constants still resolve, some digests and edges exist'. That is worth having — change 1 puts a registry query and a `Thm.prop_of` traversal in front of every constant with a non-empty ② — but it is not the three-part guarantee the sentence claims, and cost is exactly the part a reader would assume is covered.
rulings.fix: Restate PLAN.md:279 as what Test_All asserts: no crash, resolution coverage ≥ 95%, non-empty edge and digest counts. If a cost bound is wanted for change 1 — reasonable, since a registry query per constant is new work on the hit path — say so explicitly and give the budget against the figure the current run prints; otherwise drop the word 'cost'.

rulings.title: The order in which ② and ③ are concatenated is left open although it determines the digest, and the multi-info case needs one word to stay order-free
rulings.reason: Split verdict. The first half — 'say whether it is ②_sorted @ sort ③ or sort (② @ ③)' — I reject on exactly the ground the filter already used to reject elegance-4: both readings are deterministic and equally correct, no input distinguishes them, every digest in this design is an arbitrary-but-fixed function of the payload encoding, and F7 (PLAN.md:116) puts the plan's details in the implementer's hands. Consistency demands the same answer to the same question. The second half is different and does survive: when `retrieve_function_data` returns MORE than one info — the `overloading` family the revised F2 exists to serve — sorting each info's props separately and concatenating leaves the inter-info order to `Item_Net`'s serials (item_net.ML:47 `order_list o Net.unify_term`, serials assigned at :62 and re-assigned during `merge` at :66-69). Production probably cannot reach a bad case, but 'probably cannot' is precisely the shape the elegance rule tells us to replace with 'cannot', it costs one word, and the plan is already reasoning about Item_Net order two sections later in its diamond bullet (PLAN.md:246-249). The payload fold is order-sensitive (semantic_digest.ML:443), so this is not theoretical.
rulings.fix: One clause in PLAN.md §4's implementation notes, beside the existing `prop_ord` sentence: ③ means the props of ALL infos returned by the query, sorted TOGETHER by `prop_ord`, so the result never depends on the order `Item_Net.retrieve` happened to return. Do not add a ruling on the ②/③ concatenation order — that is the implementer's, on the same ground as elegance-4.

proposals_for_user: THE THREE IMPLEMENTER CHOICES ARE ALL ACCEPTED. (1) `ctxt` in the `env` record: necessary, not merely convenient — `Function_Common.retrieve_function_data` takes a `Proof.context` because `get_functions = #2 o Data.get o Context.Proof` (function_common.ML:278), and the file's whole env discipline exists to precompute per pass what would otherwise be per entity (the comment at semantic_digest.ML:33-34, :73-74); `make_env` runs once per WIP theory (semantic_store.ML:1811). One consequence to fold into the comment list: the signature comment at semantic_digest.ML:33-34 enumerates the env as exactly 'the indexed axiom table and the locale-parent index', which becomes an incomplete enumeration. (2) One shared `prop_ord` for the fallback and the new branch, with the `Defs` branch's name-only sort at :396 untouched: accepted — it is reuse rather than a second comparator, and leaving ②'s sort alone is what keeps the own-theory axioms from moving for reasons unrelated to this change. It needs the one clause of def-5. (3) A NEW numbered entry in `doc/invalidation_limitations.md` for the class 'a constant whose own definitional content does not reach its own digest': accepted — that is squarely the register's stated scope (:12-13, 已知不能覆盖的情况), it can carry honest 严重度/影响范围 values, and #6 stays the home of the dead-edge half. Its CONTENTS, though, depend on def-1: the surviving shapes must be written from the census, not from the pervasive argument alone.

THE PRE-FLIGHT CENSUS (def-1) NEEDS YOUR GO. It is one REPL evaluation — no `isabelle build`, no LMDB, the `fun_probe` shape already exists — but it is work before 开工 and it can change what gets written: whether ③ reaches `…_class.or_num` (one of the 20 record-eligible constants), whether it reaches the same-theory `overloading` family the revised F2 exists to serve, and therefore what §7's blind-spot list and §9 item 2's expected values say. The alternative is to start implementing and diagnose it afterwards, with §7 currently asserting an outcome it calls 'confirmed' on a probe that does not exist. I recommend running it first.

CHANGE 2 HAS NO STANDING IN-SUITE GUARD, ONLY A PAID ONE. After the fixes, the only thing that discriminates 'the normaliser is gone' from 'the normaliser is back' is §9 item 3 (ii) — `galmuth` must become a seed — inside the ~USD 11 acceptance. That is a genuine two-sided check (the step-10 run recorded galmuth as NOT a seed with the normaliser in place), but it is one-shot. If you want a permanent guard, it costs one signature line: export `val digest_term: term -> Term_Digest.digest128` from SEMANTIC_DIGEST (the function already exists at Tools/semantic_digest.ML:178; `val normalize` is being deleted, so the signature does not grow) and keep one assertion `digest_term t = Term_Digest.term128 t` for a term containing a `Free` and a `TFree`. It goes red the moment ANY pre-hash transform returns, not just this one. Your call whether a test-only export is acceptable — the file already has that pattern for `own_defining_axioms` (:63-65, 'exposed for the sensitivity suite'), so it would not be a new kind of thing.

`input_eqns` WAS RAISED AND I REJECT IT — for the record, so it is not re-raised a third time. `Function_Common.info` really does carry the user's equations as written (function_common.ML:29, :104), morphism-mapped (:120) and written identically by both registry writers, and taking props from it would collapse the simps/psimps case split. It must not be adopted: function.ML:74-81 takes the field from the user's spec BEFORE the sequential preprocessor runs, so for `fun` it holds the overlapping clauses rather than the disambiguated ones (VERIFICATION.md §2 row 6 measured `kraldo` producing 3 disambiguated rules), and with the sort kept, swapping two overlapping clauses — a real change of the function's value — would leave the digest unmoved. That is the very defect this plan exists to remove. The field is also read by nothing in the distribution or the shipped AFP and does not exist in Isabelle2024 at all.

OPTIONAL, REMOVES MOST OF THE COST ARGUMENT AROUND STEP (iii): take a second `env.copy` of the store immediately after §9 item 3 step (i). Step (iii) then becomes repeatable for ~USD 3 without re-paying the ~USD 8 baseline, which matters because the gate's verdicts are LLM-shaped and the plan currently has no cheap retry. Independently: acceptance_step10/REPORT.md finding 3 records that the gate's UNCHANGED path has never had a live sample — under the new ML, `galmuth` produces one for the first time. That is worth recording in ACCEPTANCE.md whichever way the verdict falls, which is exactly why it should be an observation and not a pass/fail criterion.
